content.text: As a digital creator in Tanzania, you face a significant challenge: accessing reliable payment processing for your online store. This guide will walk you through setting up a sovereign digital commerce stack using blockchain-based payments and Cloudflare infrastructure, giving you the freedom to sell your products globally.

For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The conventional payment processing platforms like Stripe and PayPal often restrict access to creators from certain countries, including Tanzania. This is where blockchain-based payments come in, offering a decentralized and borderless solution. By using cryptocurrencies like USDT on Tron, which settles in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10, you can bypass these restrictions and receive payments from anywhere in the world. This infrastructure is not only reliable but also cost-effective, making it an ideal solution for digital creators.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before you deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack, you need to have a few things in place. First, you need to choose a hosting platform like GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages, which offer free hosting solutions. You also need to select a backend logic solution like Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script, which can handle the payment processing and product delivery. Additionally, you need to set up a payment gateway like NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and offers a 0.5% fee. With these components in place, you can [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-start-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-without-stripe-honest-side-side-17|COREMERCH guide to selling]]-digital-products-crypto-step-step-17|How to]] building your stack.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

Setting up your payment and delivery pipeline is crucial for a seamless customer experience. You need to integrate your payment gateway with your backend logic solution, which will handle the payment processing and trigger the product delivery. You can use a solution like Supabase or Google Sheets to store orders and track payments. For product delivery, you can use Google Drive or Cloudflare R2, which offer free storage solutions. By automating the payment and delivery process, you can focus on creating and selling your digital products.
Blockchain-based payments offer a decentralized and borderless solution for digital creators.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you have set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can go live and start processing transactions. You need to configure your store to accept cryptocurrency payments and set up a system to handle refunds and disputes. You can use a solution like Binance P2P, which supports naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees, making it easier for customers to buy your products. With your store live, you can start selling your digital products to customers worldwide and receiving payments in cryptocurrency.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

As your store grows, you need to scale your infrastructure to handle increased traffic and sales. You can use a solution like Cloudflare Workers, which offers a scalable and serverless platform for handling backend logic. You can also use a solution like Supabase, which offers a scalable and reliable database solution for storing orders and tracking payments. By scaling your infrastructure, you can ensure that your store remains fast and reliable, even during peak traffic periods.
